name: Bergamot
character: Fresh, sparkling citrus with a soft floral, slightly peppery edge: the note that scents Earl Grey tea.
behaviour: A classic top note, bright and quick to fade. The backbone of colognes and the lift in chypres and ambers.

name: Labdanum resinoid
character: Warm, balsamic amber with leathery, honeyed and slightly animalic depth.
behaviour: A base note at the heart of amber accords, and one pillar of the classic chypre.

name: Vanillin
character: Sweet, creamy vanilla.
behaviour: Very tenacious: it lingers into the far drydown and sweetens everything around it.

origin.note: Made in the lab; the main odorant of cured vanilla beans.

name: Iso E Super
character: Soft, velvety, transparent woody-amber with a cedar-like dryness.
behaviour: Adds volume and radiance, often at high doses; on its own many people find it faint.

name: Ambroxan
character: Dry, mineral, ambergris-like warmth with a clean, slightly woody feel.
behaviour: Extremely long-lasting; gives the base diffusion and a skin-like glow.

name: Stemone
character: Green, leafy fig-leaf note with a fresh, slightly fruity edge.
behaviour: Gives fig accords their green, leafy side. Strong, so used sparingly.

name: cis-3-Hexenol
character: Intense, sharp green of freshly cut grass.
behaviour: Very volatile and very strong: used in traces for a natural green lift.

origin.note: Leaf alcohol; made in the lab, also occurs in green leaves.

name: Gamma octalactone
character: Creamy, sweet coconut.
behaviour: Adds milky, creamy facets; turns heavy in excess.

name: Gamma decalactone
character: Ripe, creamy peach.
behaviour: A strong fruity lactone: small amounts give a juicy, velvety peach effect.

name: Cedarwood Virginia
character: Dry, clean pencil-shaving wood.
behaviour: A versatile woody base that dries a blend down and gives it structure.

name: Hedione
character: Light, airy, transparent jasmine with a fresh, slightly citrusy glow.
behaviour: Adds radiance and diffusion; blends seamlessly and is used generously.

name: Phenylethyl alcohol
character: Mild, sweet, fresh rose petal with a hint of honey.
behaviour: The soft basis of many rose accords; gentle, so used in larger amounts.

origin.note: Made in the lab; a major component of rose.

name: Coumarin
character: Sweet hay, tonka bean and almond, with a warm, slightly tobacco-like feel.
behaviour: A key note of fougères and of tonka-like warmth; powerful at higher doses.

origin.note: Made in the lab; occurs naturally in tonka beans.

name: Oakmoss absolute
character: Damp, earthy forest floor: mossy, inky, slightly salty-sweet.
behaviour: The classic base of chypres and fougères and a strong fixative. Its use is restricted by IFRA because it can cause skin sensitisation.

name: Patchouli
character: Rich, dark, earthy and slightly camphorous, with sweet, woody depth.
behaviour: A tenacious base note and one pillar of the classic chypre.

name: Lavender
character: Fresh, herbal and floral, slightly camphorous.
behaviour: The heart of fougères and a classic in colognes; pairs naturally with coumarin and citrus.

name: Dihydromyrcenol
character: Fresh, clean, metallic lime-citrus with a crisp, laundry-fresh feel.
behaviour: Defines many modern fresh and fougère scents; strong and bright.

name: Cashmeran
character: Warm, musky, woody and powdery, slightly spicy: soft like cashmere.
behaviour: Adds soft, diffusive woody warmth to the heart and base.

name: Aldehyde C-11 undecylenic
character: Waxy, clean and fresh, with a fizzy, metallic sparkle.
behaviour: Strong: used in traces to add sparkle and lift, the 'aldehydic' effect.

name: Ethylene brassylate
character: Soft, sweet, powdery musk.
behaviour: A gentle, very long-lasting musk that rounds out and fixes the base.

name: Allyl amyl glycolate
character: Sharp green-fruity, pineapple-like, with a galbanum edge.
behaviour: Very strong; a little gives a juicy green lift to the top.

name: Black tea SFE
character: Dry, smoky tea leaf with hay-like and leathery facets.
behaviour: Adds a dark, dry, slightly smoky depth to the heart.

name: Beta-damascone
character: Rich, fruity rose with plum, blackcurrant and tobacco facets.
behaviour: Extremely powerful: used in traces to make roses and fruits glow.

name: Beta-ionone
character: Violet and orris, woody and slightly fruity.
behaviour: Gives violet and powdery orris effects to florals and woods.

name: Delta-decalactone
character: Creamy, milky coconut with a soft peach note.
behaviour: Adds a gentle milky creaminess to fruity and floral blends.

name: Douglas fir needle
character: Fresh, sweet conifer needles with a citrusy lift.
behaviour: A bright, resinous top note for forest and winter accords.

name: Isobornyl acetate
character: Fresh pine needles and camphor, clean and balsamic.
behaviour: A classic pine note for fresh, coniferous accords.

name: Pink peppercorn
character: Fresh, rosy, peppery-spicy with a citrus lift.
behaviour: A sparkling spicy top note; modern and bright.

name: Jasmine absolute
character: Rich, heady, sweet white floral with fruity and slightly animalic (indolic) facets.
behaviour: The great white floral of perfumery; a little gives a blend warmth and radiance.

name: Rose de mai absolute
character: Rich, honeyed, deep rose with a green, slightly waxy edge.
behaviour: The Grasse rose: fuller and more honeyed than the Bulgarian rose.

name: Tuberose absolute
character: Creamy, narcotic white floral with buttery, coconut-like and slightly green facets.
behaviour: Very powerful and creamy; dominates a blend easily.

name: Bulgarian rose oil
character: Fresh, rich rose with honeyed and slightly spicy, clove-like facets.
behaviour: Rose otto: the classic steam-distilled rose; precious and used with care.

name: Vetiver
character: Earthy, smoky, woody roots with a fresh, grapefruit-like lift.
behaviour: A deep, very tenacious base; Haitian vetiver is known for being clean and bright.

name: Vanilla absolute
character: Rich, dark, sweet vanilla with woody, smoky and boozy facets beyond plain vanillin.
behaviour: Deeper and more complex than vanillin; the beans must be cured for months first.

name: Frankincense
character: Fresh, lemony, pine-like resin with a dry, smoky, incense depth.
behaviour: Brings a cool, churchy, resinous lift; the smoky side lingers.

name: Lemon
character: Bright, sharp, zesty lemon peel: clean and mouth-watering.
behaviour: A fast, fresh opening. Cold-pressed lemon oil can make skin react to sunlight, so it is limited in leave-on products.

name: Sweet orange
character: Sweet, juicy orange peel, cheerful and round.
behaviour: A soft, sweet citrus top note that fades quickly; cheap and friendly in colognes.

name: Grapefruit
character: Juicy, bitter grapefruit with a faintly sulphurous, sweaty edge that reads as real fruit.
behaviour: Brightens an opening and adds a modern, tart freshness.

name: Lime (distilled)
character: Sharp, fizzy, candied lime, greener than lemon.
behaviour: Distilled lime oil gives a bright, sherbet-like top note.

name: Mandarin
character: Sweet, juicy mandarin with a soft, slightly floral peel note.
behaviour: Rounder and sweeter than orange; lovely in colognes and children-of-summer accords.

name: Petitgrain bigarade
character: Green, woody-floral bitter orange leaves and twigs, with a fresh, slightly bitter edge.
behaviour: Bridges citrus and neroli; a classic part of eau de cologne.

name: Neroli
character: Fresh, honeyed, green orange blossom with a bitter, slightly metallic sparkle.
behaviour: The luminous heart of classic colognes; expensive, so used with care.

name: Citral
character: Intensely sharp, sweet lemon: lemongrass more than lemon peel.
behaviour: Gives lemony lift but is unstable in some bases and is a known skin sensitiser.

origin.note: Aldehyde found in lemongrass and lemon; also made synthetically.

name: Rosemary
character: Fresh, camphoraceous, woody herb with a cool, slightly medicinal lift.
behaviour: Adds a brisk herbal top note; a traditional partner to citrus in colognes.

name: Clary sage
character: Herbaceous, tea-like and slightly ambery, with a musky, almost leathery warmth.
behaviour: Softens and warms fougères and lavender accords.

name: Peppermint
character: Cool, sweet, unmistakable mint.
behaviour: Very recognisable; a little gives coolness, a lot smells of toothpaste.

name: Basil
character: Green, sweet, anise-like herb with a peppery freshness.
behaviour: Adds a culinary green freshness to citrus and floral tops.

name: Lavandin grosso
character: Lavender with a sharper, more camphoraceous and woody edge.
behaviour: A cheaper, bolder cousin of lavender; good in fougères and soaps.

name: Linalool
character: Fresh, light, floral-woody, a little like lavender and bergamot without the citrus.
behaviour: One of the most used materials in perfumery: it freshens and blends almost anything.

origin.note: Found in lavender, coriander and rosewood; made in quantity synthetically.

name: Linalyl acetate
character: Fresh, fruity, bergamot-lavender ester, soft and clean.
behaviour: Gives the sweet, fruity side of lavender and bergamot.

origin.note: Ester found in lavender and bergamot; also synthetic.

name: Galbanum
character: Intensely green, bitter and resinous, like snapped stems and green peppers.
behaviour: Very powerful: a drop gives a sharp, natural green opening.

name: Violet leaf absolute
character: Leafy and green, like cucumber skin and wet earth, with a faint violet sweetness.
behaviour: Potent; gives a dewy green freshness in tiny amounts.

name: Ligustral (Triplal)
character: Sharp, leafy, green-grassy aldehyde with a hint of citrus.
behaviour: A strong green kick; a little goes a long way.

name: cis-3-Hexenyl acetate
character: Sharp, sweet green: unripe banana and fresh-cut leaves.
behaviour: Makes green notes juicier and fruitier than hexenol alone.

name: Geranium
character: Rosy, minty-green and slightly fruity, like crushed geranium leaves.
behaviour: A rose helper and a staple of fougères and masculine florals.

name: Ylang-ylang extra
character: Sweet, creamy, heady flower with banana and spice facets.
behaviour: Rich and narcotic: rounds out florals and orientals.

name: Orange flower absolute
character: Heady, honeyed, slightly indolic orange blossom, richer and warmer than neroli.
behaviour: A luxurious white-floral heart.

name: Orris butter
character: Powdery, buttery violet and rooty carrot, cool and refined.
behaviour: One of the most precious materials; the rhizomes are aged for years before extraction.

name: Mimosa absolute
character: Powdery, honeyed, slightly green flower with a soft cucumber edge.
behaviour: Gives a sunny, powdery softness.

name: Benzyl acetate
character: Sweet, fruity-floral, like jasmine and pear drops.
behaviour: The main component of jasmine; brightens white florals.

origin.note: Ester found in jasmine and ylang-ylang; synthetic.

name: Hydroxycitronellal
character: Soft, fresh, sweet lily of the valley.
behaviour: A classic muguet material; restricted because it can sensitise skin.

name: Helional
character: Watery, green, cyclamen-like floral with an airy, ozonic freshness.
behaviour: Adds air and transparency to florals.

name: Geraniol
character: Sweet, rosy and slightly citrusy.
behaviour: A building block of rose accords; restricted as a possible sensitiser.

origin.note: Found in rose and geranium oils; also synthetic.

name: Citronellol
character: Fresh, waxy, rosy, a little citrusy.
behaviour: With phenylethyl alcohol and geraniol, the backbone of a rose accord.

origin.note: Found in rose and geranium oils; also synthetic.

name: Heliotropin
character: Powdery, almondy and vanillic, like cherry pie and heliotrope flowers.
behaviour: Gives a soft, powdery sweetness; a classic of old-fashioned powders.

name: Methyl ionone
character: Powdery orris and violet with a soft woody warmth.
behaviour: Gives an orris effect without the price; a staple of powdery florals.

name: Indole
character: Neat, it smells of mothballs and animal; in a trace, it makes white flowers heady and alive.
behaviour: Present in jasmine and orange blossom. Always used very diluted.

origin.note: Found in jasmine and orange blossom; synthetic.

name: Benzyl salicylate
character: Faint, sweet, balsamic-floral, like warm skin in the sun.
behaviour: Barely smells on its own but rounds and fixes florals.

origin.note: Synthetic; also in some flower absolutes.

name: Rose oxide
character: Metallic, green, geranium-like rose with a fresh lift.
behaviour: Very strong: a trace gives a natural, dewy rose top.

origin.note: Found in rose and geranium oils; synthetic.

name: Raspberry ketone
character: Sweet raspberry jam with a soft, slightly woody warmth.
behaviour: Lasting fruitiness for berry accords.

name: Aldehyde C-14 (peach)
character: Creamy, velvety peach skin.
behaviour: Despite the name it is a lactone (gamma-undecalactone). Famous in early-20th-century chypres.

name: Aldehyde C-18 (coconut)
character: Creamy, sweet coconut.
behaviour: Despite the name it is a lactone (gamma-nonalactone).

name: Allyl caproate
character: Sweet, juicy pineapple.
behaviour: A bright fruity top note.

name: Blackcurrant bud absolute
character: Green, fruity blackcurrant with a sharp, catty, sulphurous edge.
behaviour: Gives a tart, natural cassis effect.

name: Clove bud
character: Warm, sweet, spicy clove, like mulled wine.
behaviour: A classic warm spice; restricted because its eugenol can sensitise skin.

name: Cardamom
character: Fresh, sweet, camphoraceous spice with a eucalyptus-like coolness.
behaviour: Bright, airy spice for openings.

name: Black pepper
character: Dry, woody, piney pepper, fresh rather than hot.
behaviour: Gives a lively, dry spice to openings.

name: Nutmeg
character: Warm, sweet, woody spice with a fresh, slightly terpenic lift.
behaviour: Warms a fougère or woody accord.

name: Ginger
character: Fresh, lemony, warm and slightly woody root.
behaviour: Sparkling spice for openings.

name: Eugenol
character: Spicy, sweet, warm clove.
behaviour: The main smell of clove; restricted as a possible sensitiser.

name: Aldehyde C-10 (decanal)
character: Waxy, fatty orange peel.
behaviour: Makes citrus tops brighter and more lifelike.

name: Aldehyde C-12 lauric
character: Waxy, soapy, clean, with a violet and pine-needle edge.
behaviour: The "clean linen" sparkle of classic aldehydic florals.

name: Aldehyde C-12 MNA
character: Waxy and herbaceous with an ambergris-like, incense warmth.
behaviour: Gives aldehydic florals their rich, metallic radiance.

name: Sandalwood
character: Soft, creamy, milky wood with a sweet, buttery warmth.
behaviour: A gentle, long-lasting base. Indian sandalwood was over-harvested; most now comes from managed plantations.

name: Guaiac wood
character: Smoky, rosy, slightly tea-like wood.
behaviour: Adds a soft smoke to woody bases.

name: Cypress
character: Fresh, resinous, green conifer with a smoky dryness.
behaviour: A crisp coniferous lift for chypres and fougères.

name: Atlas cedarwood
character: Sweet, honeyed, slightly balsamic cedar, softer than Virginia cedar.
behaviour: A warm, lasting woody base.

name: Javanol
character: Powerful, creamy, rosy sandalwood.
behaviour: A modern sandalwood molecule, strong enough to use in traces.

name: Vertofix
character: Dry, woody-ambery, vetiver-like and slightly leathery.
behaviour: A cheap, lasting dry-woody base.

origin.note: Methyl cedryl ketone, made from cedarwood oil.

name: Birch tar (rectified)
character: Smoky, tarry, leathery: a campfire and a new saddle.
behaviour: The traditional heart of Russian-leather accords. Only refined grades are allowed.

name: Cypriol
character: Smoky, earthy, woody root, a little like vetiver and leather.
behaviour: Adds dark, dry depth to woody bases.

name: Isobutyl quinoline
character: Harsh, green, earthy leather.
behaviour: Very strong; the leathery bite in classic leather and chypre accords.

name: Benzoin Siam
character: Sweet, warm, vanilla-like balsam.
behaviour: A soft, sweet fixative in ambers and orientals.

name: Myrrh
character: Warm, bitter, mushroomy resin with a slightly medicinal edge.
behaviour: Gives depth and a churchy darkness to resinous bases.

name: Opoponax
character: Sweet, warm, honeyed balsam with a powdery, spicy edge.
behaviour: Rich and ambery; a classic oriental base.

name: Tonka absolute
character: Sweet hay, almond and caramel: coumarin with a warm, rounded naturalness.
behaviour: A cozy, sweet base; its coumarin is restricted.

name: Ethyl vanillin
character: Sweeter, creamier and about three times stronger than vanillin.
behaviour: Gives a rich vanilla with less material.

name: Ethyl maltol
character: Sweet, caramelised sugar and candy floss.
behaviour: The fairground-sweet note of modern gourmands.

name: Cocoa absolute
character: Dark, dusty cocoa powder, bitter and warm.
behaviour: A rich, dark gourmand note.

name: Benzaldehyde
character: Bitter almond and cherry.
behaviour: A sweet, nutty top note.

origin.note: Found in bitter almond oil; synthetic.

name: Galaxolide
character: Clean, sweet, powdery musk: the smell of fresh laundry.
behaviour: One of the most used musks; soft and long-lasting.

name: Habanolide
character: Clean, slightly metallic, warm musk, like hot ironed sheets.
behaviour: A modern macrocyclic musk.

name: Helvetolide
character: Fruity, pear-like, powdery musk.
behaviour: A modern musk with a soft fruity lift.

name: Ambrettolide
character: Musky, fruity, wine-like and powdery: the musk of ambrette seed.
behaviour: A luxurious, natural-smelling musk.

origin.note: Macrocyclic musk found in ambrette seed.

name: Ambrette seed
character: Musky, pear-like and slightly winey: a plant musk.
behaviour: A rare natural musk, once the vegetable alternative to animal musks.

name: Exaltolide
character: Elegant, powdery, slightly animalic musk.
behaviour: One of the first macrocyclic musks.

name: Treemoss absolute
character: Inky, woody, slightly turpentine-like moss, sharper than oakmoss.
behaviour: Strictly limited; adds a dark, mossy depth to chypres.

name: Evernyl
character: Earthy, woody, oakmoss-like, dry and powdery.
behaviour: A key synthetic for chypres now that oakmoss is restricted.

origin.note: Methyl atrarate (veramoss), a component of oakmoss.
